title: The Writings of Clement of Alexandria, Vol. 2
author: Clement of Alexandria (Wilson trans)
description: The Writings of Clement of Alexandria, Volume 2, translated by William Wilson, in the Ante-Nicene Christian Library (Edinburgh: T. & T. Clark, 1869). This volume continues the Miscellanies (Stromata), Clement's sprawling, deliberately unsystematic 'patchwork' of reflections, in which he argues that Greek philosophy was a preparation for the Gospel, that true knowledge (gnosis) builds on faith, and that the perfect Christian gnostic is passionless, loving and assimilated to God. He discusses symbolism and esoteric teaching in Egyptian, Pythagorean and biblical traditions, the 'theft' of the Greeks from Hebrew wisdom, marriage, martyrdom and the critique of heretical Gnostics such as Basilides and Valentinus. It also includes Who Is the Rich Man That Shall Be Saved? and fragments, among them the Excerpts from Theodotus preserving Valentinian teaching. It is essential for Christian gnosis and early esotericism.
